headline: Three levels split the field by what happens to the class chain: the css-prop fold concatenates it into one class and ties `vanilla`, while every atomic lane pays a merge per level.

microbench.why: Three levels ask each library what it does with a chain of classes. The css-prop fold merges the whole chain into a single class on the plain element and ties `vanilla` at 0.517 against 0.509 ms/1k; the styled fold trails at 0.686 because a residual `Yak` survives the `styled(Component)` seam. The atomic lanes cannot merge for free: `stylex-layers` runs `styleq` per element and slides from 0.530 ms/1k at one level to 0.934 here, `bamboo` joins three literals through `cx()` and goes 0.508 to 0.793, and `panda` re-resolves every level's object for 9.72. The 9.6.0 runtime is the counter-example at 2.40 ms/1k, one `Yak` render per level.

autocannon.why: The concatenated class serves 1541 req/s and `vanilla` 1525. The styled fold's residual wrapper holds it to 1188, and `bamboo`'s three `cx()` joins put it at 828 next to `cnfast`'s 824. `panda` collapses to 85 req/s, re-resolving three merged objects per element on every request.

attribution.why: `next-yak-css-9.7` renders in 0.626 ms with a 0.274 ms library slice, which is `vanilla`'s 0.623 within noise. `panda` puts 12.4 of its 13.3 ms into component self-time. `stylex-layers` shows the atomic merge directly, 0.211 ms of library slice plus 0.349 ms of component self-time where the flat button had none, and `bamboo`'s slice stays at zero while its 0.862 ms goes to react-dom writing a class string that now carries all three levels.

hydrate.why: Static sheets hydrate as pure JS, 48.1-50.7 ms with no style or layout in the span. `goober` (106 ms) and `styled-components` (103 ms) inject and pay 0.22 ms of recalc plus a layout pass, and `panda` at 94.1 ms re-resolves its objects on the client. Spreads inside the fast cluster reach 49%, so it is a tie.

inp.why: Re-rendering three nested components costs 0.40-0.68 ms of JS in every build-time lane, and they span 6.5-8.2 ms, less than the repeat-to-repeat spread. `panda` re-resolves three merged objects and needs 37.2 ms, `goober` 11.1 and `emotion` 9.9. Depth reaches the interaction only where the class is computed at render.

mount.why: Cold mount puts the concatenated-class lane at `vanilla`'s level, 73.9 against 73.7 ms, with the atomic lanes just behind (`bamboo` 79.6, `stylex-layers` 83.7) as the browser matches more classes per element. `panda` (125 ms), `emotion` (113 ms), `goober` (107 ms) and `styled-components` (101 ms) do their styling before first paint.

renderTiming.why: One recalculation and one layout everywhere, so only the recalc cost (0.133-0.186 ms) orders the lanes. Composition changes how many classes an element carries, not how often Chrome recalculates a static sheet.

payload.why: One class for the whole chain means payload does not grow with depth: `next-yak-css-9.7` ships 2.66 kB gzipped here against 2.67 at one level. The atomic lanes append each level's classes to the attribute instead, `bamboo` rising 4.94 to 5.33 kB and `stylex-layers` 5.62 to 5.84. `styled-components` (16.5 kB) and `cnfast` (15.1 kB) carry a runtime or a scanned sheet that dwarfs both.

nsweep.why: At 4000 three-level instances the concatenated class tracks `vanilla`, 2.11 against 2.09 ms. `bamboo` (3.35 ms) and `stylex-layers` (3.82 ms) carry their per-level merge into the sweep and `panda` reaches 44.5 ms. The 9.6.0 runtime's 9.81 ms is three `Yak` renders per instance multiplied by n.

crossCase: The middle of the composition ladder (the Examples `compose-1` and `compose-6` are its siblings). The css-prop fold holds `vanilla`'s cost at every depth (0.522, 0.517, 0.517 ms/1k) and a flat 2.66-2.67 kB payload, because the chain collapses into one class name. Depth is what the atomic lanes pay for: `bamboo` climbs 0.508 to 0.793 to 1.12 ms/1k and `stylex-layers` 0.530 to 0.934 to 1.36, since every level brings another merge and another class token.
